articles.title: We read Sofia Franklyn’s memoir about her falling-out with Alex Cooper so you don’t have to
articles.summary: “Daddy Issues” is a tell-all from Franklyn’s side about the end of her business relationship and friendship with Cooper, who went on to helm “Call Her Daddy”...
articles.body:
The "Daddy Gang" is finally getting to hear from the co-"founding father" of "Call Her Daddy."

Sofia Franklyn, who co-created the famous podcast with Alex Cooper, on Tuesday released her memoir, "Daddy Issues," in which she details her falling-out with her now ex-friend.

The duo shot to viral fame in 2018, when the podcast was still under Barstool Sports. It became known for candid conversations about commonly taboo topics for women to discuss publicly, including raunchy sex stories.

But the two professionally split up in 2020, news that initially shocked their listeners. Cooper went on to host the podcast solo, eventually moving it to Spotify and now SiriusXM in lucrative deals that helped propel her to mainstream success.

Meanwhile, Franklyn, who is an influencer with over 619,000 Instagram followers, launched her own podcast titled "Sofia with an F."

Over the years, rumors had circulated about what exactly happened between Franklyn and Cooper. Here are some of the biggest claims in Franklyn's 240-page book.

Franklyn writes about struggling to find a clear path as she was growing up in Utah with a single mom. She was arrested three times: once for using a fake ID and twice for underage drinking. Eventually, she left to start anew in New York City, largely to escape an abusive relationship.

But her early days in the city were far from ideal. She lived with her aunt and was working at Morgan Stanley in a job under a toxic boss who she claims harassed her regularly. She eventually moved into her own place, which she could barely afford, and found herself feeling extremely lonely.

A random girl Franklyn befriended in a ride-share connected her to Cooper and her childhood friend Lauren, who were looking for a third roommate.

Cooper and Franklyn ended up becoming inseparable, with Lauren largely out of the picture as she spent much of her time with her boyfriend. But one night, Franklyn writes, she and Lauren shared a rare evening in the apartment alone together.

That's when Lauren asked Franklyn whether she thought it was weird that Cooper had "tossed" her aside.

"You showed up and it was like I never existed," Franklyn said Lauren told her, which prompted Franklyn to apologize.

Lauren also told Franklyn that Cooper "uses you because you're hot, to like, go to parties and stuff."

At the time, Franklyn wrote, she felt defensive of her friendship with Cooper and did not think of Cooper as "using" her.

But later, another close friend of Cooper's from childhood also seemed to warn her that Cooper was not going to stick with her.

Muji, known to early "Call Her Daddy" listeners as "Milfhunter," worked on the podcast with the duo. He told Franklyn that Cooper "doesn't have friends. I've watched it happen since high school."

When Cooper abruptly fired Muji, Franklyn said, he told her: "She's gonna f--- you."

An alleged firing attempt, secret raise and IP disagreement

Cooper and Franklyn's stars rose quickly at Barstool as the two took creative control of their show with company founder Dave Portnoy's blessing.

But Franklyn started to feel things change after the Barstool holiday party. That night, she felt "insane anxiety," drank excessively and fought with Cooper.

An angry Cooper told Franklyn she was "rude" and "aggressive" toward her at the party and that everyone, including Portnoy, had noticed and wanted to fire her.

Franklyn says she wanted to apologize to Portnoy for her behavior but was told not to by Cooper. When she finally did say something, Portnoy appeared to dismiss it, saying that "the girls got in a fight."

It wasn't until later, Franklyn writes, that she learned Cooper had used the party as a way to negotiate a raise for herself.

Muji purportedly told her that Cooper said, "If I have to put up with her, I need more money." She got the raise: $20,000 more than Franklyn every year.

"She didn't tell you because she didn't want you to know she tried to get you fired," Franklyn said Muji told her.

Franklyn writes that in 2020, when the duo were negotiating their new contract together, they sent Barstool an email with a new proposal asking for a "50/50 split of all revenue derived from Barstool's exploitation of the property (i.e., advertisers, sponsors, merch, etc.)" and a "minimum guarantee — $1M each, per year."

The negotiations centered on the intellectual property for "Call Her Daddy," which Barstool Sports owned and could technically continue without Franklyn or Cooper attached.

Amid their talks with Barstool, Franklyn said, she and Cooper agreed their goal was to stay together. They even came up with a spinoff podcast in case the negotiations fell through, titling it "The Fathers."

"We're being corny as s---, but it's because we're both blissed out on the plan and our future — we don't know how Barstool will respond, but we know that staying together is more important than losing the IP, or whatever they may threaten. What is the name without us?"

But in the end, Franklyn was ousted as co-host. Portnoy called Franklyn to tell her that Cooper had met with him separately and proposed going on without her.

"She came to me with a plan, and I needed an episode. There's no clear favorite," he told her, according to Franklyn's memoir. "You could always have your own show, and we promote the s--- out of it like we did with Call Her Daddy . I think it would be huge."

Portnoy also said Cooper had hired her own lawyer and claimed that Franklyn had been "the one that's been dragging this on, and she's been ready to sign this thing."

Franklyn claims Cooper subsequently locked her out of their shared social accounts and posted a 52-minute YouTube breakup video called " The Truth about Call Her Daddy " in which she described Franklyn as a "liability." Six years later, the video is still up, and it has amassed 4.6 million views.

Representatives for Portnoy and Cooper did not respond to requests for comment Tuesday.

The book opens with a scene in which Franklyn's book agent calls her to say she had received an angry call from Matt Kaplan.

Kaplan, a Hollywood producer, married Cooper in 2024. The couple co-founded the Unwell Network, a subsidiary of the media company Trending.

Franklyn writes that her agent told her Kaplan said Cooper would sue.

Representatives from Unwell told The New York Times that Kaplan "never discussed the book's claims or any intent to sue the author with Verve."

A representative for Kaplan did not respond to a request for comment Tuesday.

articles.title: Dani García, chef: “La ensalada césar más rica no se hace con lechuga, sino con tomate azul, dos yemas de huevo, dos anchoas y 30 gramos de queso parmesano rallado”
articles.standfirst: El cocinero marbellí reinventa el clásico con el tomate como protagonista
articles.summary: El cocinero marbellí reinventa el clásico con el tomate como protagonista
articles.body: La ensalada césar es uno de esos platos que casi nadie se atreve a tocar. Lechuga romana, picatostes, parmesano y su inconfundible salsa forman una combinación que se repite en restaurantes de medio mundo. Dani García, sin embargo, ha decidido darle la vuelta. El chef andaluz ha compartido en sus redes una versión en la que la lechuga desaparece y el tomate pasa a ocupar el centro del plato. Tras años preparándola de la forma clásica, el cocinero se plantea una pregunta sencilla: “¿Por qué no hacerla con un gran tomate?”. Para su receta elige el tomate azul, una variedad que llama la atención por el tono violeta oscuro, casi negro, de su piel. Si no se encuentra, propone alternativas como el rosa de Barbastro o el raf. Lo importante es que esté maduro pero firme, ya que se corta en láminas muy finas y un tomate blando terminaría deshecho. El secreto está, como en la receta original, en el aliño. Para dos tomates hacen falta dos yemas de huevo, 30 mililitros de aceite de oliva virgen extra, unas gotas de zumo de limón, una cucharadita de mostaza, dos filetes de anchoa en salazón y 30 gramos de parmesano rallado. El primer paso es triturar las anchoas hasta convertirlas en una especie de puré. Después se añaden las yemas y la mostaza y se va incorporando el aceite poco a poco para montar una emulsión, que se termina con el limón y el queso. Solo queda cortar los tomates y cubrirlos con la salsa. Quien prefiera no usar huevo crudo puede recurrir a yemas pasteurizadas, que se venden en muchos supermercados y funcionan igual. El resultado conserva la esencia de la César, con el punto salino de la anchoa y la cremosidad del huevo, pero con la frescura del tomate. Una versión que, curiosamente, se aleja del original creado en 1924 en Tijuana por el italiano Caesar Cardini, que tampoco llevaba anchoas.

articles.title: I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! 2026 - see the line-up in full
articles.summary: The football star will be joined by Gavin and Stacey star Joanna Page and YouTuber Sharky among others.
articles.body:
Former England and Manchester United footballer Wayne Rooney, Gavin and Stacey star Joanna Page and YouTuber Sharky will be among the intrepid crew entering the jungle Down Under for this year's I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out Of Here!

They will be joined by Kaiser Chiefs frontman Ricky Wilson, Paralympian and presenter Ade Adepitan, actress Claire Sweeney and broadcaster Mariella Frostrup.

TV presenter AJ Odudu, comedian Jack Skipper, Love Island contestant Chloe Burrows and model Leomie Anderson round out the team headed for Australia.

Hosts Ant and Dec will return with the ITV show's opening episode on Monday, 16 November, with the series now in its 26th year.

Ade Adepitan - Paralympian and documentary maker, who will be the first wheelchair user in the show's history

Leomie Anderson - Model and co-host of Glow Up: Britain's Next Make-Up Star

Chloe Burrows - Love Island finalist, Kiss Radio breakfast presenter and host of Chloe vs The World podcast

Mariella Frostrup - Broadcaster, author and journalist, including appearances on Loose Women and Times Radio

AJ Odudu - Big Brother presenter and former Strictly Come Dancing contestant

Joanna Page - Stacey from hit sitcom Gavin and Stacey, and host of TV series including Shift the Thrift and Shop Well For Less

Wayne Rooney - Former Everton, Manchester United and England striker turned football manager and pundit

Sharky - one of YouTube's Beta Squad (alongside Celebrity Traitors star King Kenny among others), who have 12 million subscribers

Jack Skipper - Stand-up comedian and social media star

Claire Sweeney - Coronation Street and Brookside star and musical actress

Ricky Wilson - Kaiser Chiefs singer, ex-Virgin Radio drivetime host and former The Voice UK coach

Rooney is following in the footsteps of his wife Coleen, who was runner-up on I'm A Celebrity in 2024.

"If you're going in you want to win it," he said. "Coleen's already tried and obviously she finished second in the show so I'm here to bring that title back to the Rooney household."

Rooney admitted that jumping out of a helicopter is his biggest fear. "I've been booked to jump out of a plane three times before and never made it on the plane," he said.

"I don't like snakes or what is in the water either - I don't go in the sea."

Producers are making adaptations to the Australian jungle camp so it is accessible for Adepitan.

In a press statement, he said: "For me, this is a moment in time. Even if I go out in the first week, I will always be remembered as the person in a wheelchair. I am slightly overwhelmed. It's never been done before, and it never crossed my mind I would be the first."

Keith Lemon comedian Leigh Francis is not among the official line-up but is rumoured to become a late addition.

The last I'm A Celebrity series was the all-star version in South Africa, which was marked by heated arguments and walk-outs among the cast during the live final in April.

articles.title: Katy Perry's comment that ex 'should be in jail' resurfaces after Russell Brand's prison sentencing
articles.summary: From Kate Moss to Katy Perry to wife Laura Gallacher Brand, Russell Brand's romantic history spans high-profile romances and a headline-making divorce.
articles.body: Russell Brand's romantic past is drawing renewed attention following his prison sentencing, including ex-wife Katy Perry's description of his behavior during their marriage as "very controlling." Years before the comedian was convicted of rape and sexual assault, Perry said Brand struggled with her role as "the boss" of her own career and shared how their whirlwind marriage ended with a text message in which he announced he wanted a divorce. Now, her past comments are resurfacing alongside renewed interest in Brand’s relationship history, from his brief romance with Spice Girls singer Geri Halliwell to his marriage to his current wife Laura Brand, who testified in his defense. RUSSELL BRAND SENTENCED AFTER RAPE, SEXUAL ASSAULT CONVICTIONS IN UK Here's a look back at Brand's most notable relationships. Kate Moss — 2006 Brand described a brief romantic encounter with Kate Moss in his memoir, "Booky Wook 2: This Time It's Personal," writing that their connection elevated his celebrity status. "I could never have anticipated the instant elevation that this liaison would afford me, it was like being awarded a celebrity Victoria Cross," he wrote, according to the New York Post. The comedian, who met Moss through a mutual friend, expressed his admiration for the model in the book. "Kate Moss is the prettiest girl in all our schools," he wrote. "Behold our queen, but don’t look at her directly or all else you gaze upon till death brings down your lids will be as shadows compared to her beauty." In the book, Brand wrote that he became smitten, but their connection faded after he publicly downplayed the encounter to journalists. Teresa Palmer — 2008 Brand and Australian actress Teresa Palmer briefly dated after meeting while filming "Bedtime Stories" in 2008. By July of that year, both were publicly discussing their relationship, with Brand suggesting he was ready to leave his womanizing reputation behind. "I’m a changed man," he said at the time, according to Cosmopolitan. "I’ve met someone very beautiful and I’ve settled down." Palmer expressed similar enthusiasm about their budding romance. "We’ve only been together for a month, but it’s going brilliantly," she said, according to the outlet. The pair attended the O2 Silver Clef Awards together in London on July 4, 2008, but their relationship was short-lived. By the fall of 2008, the couple had separated. KATY PERRY SNUBS FAMOUS EXES BEFORE SWEET NOD TO JUSTIN TRUDEAU IN CHEEKY ONSTAGE MOMENT Katy Perry — 2009–2012 Brand and Katy Perry, who met on the set of "Get Him to the Greek" in 2009, announced their engagement in January 2010 before marrying in India on Oct. 23 of that year. Their marriage lasted approximately 14 months before Brand filed for divorce in December 2011. Perry later discussed their relationship in a 2013 Vogue interview, describing behavior she considered "controlling." KATY PERRY FIGHTS BACK AGAINST RUBY ROSE'S 'CATEGORICALLY FALSE' SEXUAL ASSAULT ALLEGATIONS "He didn’t like the atmosphere of me being the boss on tour. So that was really hurtful, and it was very controlling, which was upsetting," she said. "I felt a lot of responsibility for it ending, but then I found out the real truth, which I can’t necessarily disclose because I keep it locked in my safe for a rainy day. I let go, and I was like: This isn’t because of me, this is beyond me. So I have moved on from that." During the interview, Perry said Brand informed her of his divorce plans by text message. The moment she received the message was captured on camera and featured in the pop star's 2012 documentary "Katy Perry: Part of Me." Following Brand's sentencing, another video showing an interaction between Brand and Perry gained traction online. During an interview at the 2010 Vanity Fair Oscar party, Brand appeared to criticize Perry for swearing on camera and displayed a badge bearing the word "Obey." "He didn’t like her getting more attention than him," one social media user wrote on X. Months before his conviction, Perry made a pointed remark about an ex during a concert in July at Blenheim Palace in Oxfordshire, England. While playing an interactive game that asked audience members to act out their reaction to seeing an ex, Perry said, "I hope my ex isn’t here. He should be in jail," according to The Mirror. Perry did not specifically name Brand. Isabella Brewster — Summer 2012 Brand began dating Isabella Brewster, a former talent agent, following his split from Perry. The pair reportedly met at a yoga class. He confirmed their romance during a July 18, 2012, appearance on Howard Stern's radio show, just days after his divorce became final. "Some things in the newspaper aren’t true … that’s true, actually," Brand said when asked about Brewster, according to E! News. PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE Their relationship appeared to move quickly. According to Cosmopolitan, the pair were reportedly considering renting a home together in Los Angeles. By late August, however, the romance had ended. "Isabella and [Russell] broke it off," a source told Us Weekly at the time. "He has been in London since the Olympics and is traveling for standup." Geri Halliwell — August 2012 Following his split from Brewster, Brand was briefly linked to Spice Girls singer Geri Halliwell. The pair reportedly grew close during preparations for the 2012 London Olympics' closing ceremony, at which both performed. They were photographed holding hands during a visit to Hampton Court Palace with Halliwell’s daughter, Bluebell, and were also reportedly spotted enjoying a picnic on Hampstead Heath. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Despite the attention surrounding their budding romance, the relationship reportedly ended within weeks. "He isn’t ready to settle down so soon after coming out of marriage," a source told The Mirror. Jemima Goldsmith — 2013–2014 Brand began dating producer and journalist Jemima Goldsmith in 2013. Their relationship lasted approximately a year, during which the comedian publicly expressed his love for her and said their connection felt different from his previous romances. "I really love her. I’m very, very happy in a relationship that feels very different from anything I’ve experienced before," Brand reportedly said during a 2014 appearance on "The Jonathan Ross Show." Their breakup was reported in September 2014. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE In November 2026, Goldsmith spoke publicly about her relationship with Brand, offering a different account of her experience with him. In a statement posted on X following his sentencing, she accused him of "violence, coercive control and abuse." She alleged that she had called police to have him removed from her home during a violent incident in 2014. Goldsmith said she chose not to pursue charges or speak publicly at the time because she feared the impact of media attention on her teenage children. "I have neither seen nor spoken to Brand since that period in 2014," she wrote. Laura Gallacher Brand — 2006–2007; reunited in 2015, married in 2017 Brand’s relationship with his current wife, Laura Gallacher Brand, began years before his marriage to Perry. Gallacher, an author and illustrator whose sister is British broadcaster Kirsty Gallacher, first became involved with Brand in 2006. She was 19 and he was 31. Their initial relationship ended the following year amid his reported difficulty with monogamy. "When I met him, I was aware that he liked women, and I was aware toward the latter half of that year that he was engaging with other women," Laura told the court during Brand's trial, according to Sky News. "I was not interested in having a relationship with him if he was sleeping with other people. I was invested; we both had told each other we loved each other, but it was clear it was difficult for him to be monogamous." After Brand’s marriage to Perry ended, he and Laura reconnected in 2015. The couple welcomed daughter Mabel in November 2016 before marrying on Aug. 26, 2017, in a ceremony near Henley-on-Thames, England. Their family later grew with the birth of their daughter Peggy in July 2018 and a son in 2023. Laura publicly defended her husband during his 2026 rape and sexual assault trial. Laura described Brand as "caring and kind, a wonderful father to our children and an amazing, attentive husband," adding that he has an "eye for detail I have never known before." I love him very much."

articles.title: I'm a Celebrity: Gavin and Stacey's Joanna Page gets message from Nessa
articles.summary: Ruth Jones sends a message from 'Nessa' to co-star Joanna Page as Page prepares for her jungle debut.
articles.body:
Gavin and Stacey star Joanna Page has confirmed she will appear on the upcoming reality TV series I'm a Celebrity, with her former co-star Ruth Jones urging her to "have a crackin' time".

Page, who played Stacey Shipman in the BBC comedy, is joining this year's line-up of celebrities on the forthcoming show in Australia.

The 49-year-old, from Swansea, said she had her sights on becoming the first Welsh Queen of the Jungle.

"You makes Barry very proud, I'm not gonna lie," said Jones - assuming her former Gavin & Stacey character Nessa Jenkins - on Instagram.

"They're gonna make you stick all manner of matter in your gob. And I'm not talking Gwen's omelettes... Just don't over do it, alrigh'? You knows what a weak constitution you has."

Speaking ahead of her trip down under, Page said she believed her co-stars will be "shocked" when she arrives in the jungle for the ITV reality show.

"I also know they will find it funny. They know exactly what I am like and they will laugh."

Page said being the first Welsh queen would be a "pretty good title to take home", but added she was just as excited to see how long she could last.

"I'm going to see this to the end and I'm going to be strong. I am going to get the most out of this."

As a mother-of-four, Page said she hoped her part in the show will help her "reconnect" with who she was before becoming a mum.

"This is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. I'm very much an impulsive person and I just make a gut decision, so I said 'yes' straight away," said Page.

She said she hoped to find "peace and time for my thoughts" away from the everyday worries about feeding the children and getting everyone ready for the school run.

"I can be me, I can be Jo and not just mummy all the time. I think that will be nice."

"I will never get to do anything like this again. I am telling myself, 'Come on Jo, let's take yourself off to Australia and give yourself an experience'.

"It's exciting and it's going to be life-changing."

Page will enter the jungle alongside footballer Wayne Rooney, TV personality Chloe Burrows and soap star Claire Sweeney.

Rooney will follow in his wife Coleen's footsteps after she finished as runner-up on the 2024 series, and said he hoped "people will see me for who I am".

He said he had "always wanted to do" the show, joking that because of his short-lived football managerial career, he had more time on his hands.

"I like to have fun and I like to think I am actually a fun guy to be around.

"I do like to mess around a bit and I do talk a lot. People will have their own opinions, but I hope they will see me as a genuine person."

Page will be also joined by Paralympian and TV presenter Ade Adepitan - who will be the first contestant in a wheelchair to appear on the show – something he said his eight-year-old self would not believe.

"Words like 'honour' and 'privilege' are the ones I feel, but I don't think they sum it up enough," he said.

"For me, this is a moment in time. Even if I go out in the first week, I will always be remembered as the person in a wheelchair. I am slightly overwhelmed.

"It's never been done before, and it never crossed my mind I would be the first.

I'm A Celebrity… Get Me Out Of Here! starts on Monday, 16 November at 21:00 GMT on ITV.

articles.title: Un piquete entra en el plató de Gemma Nierga en RTVE y obliga a suspender ‘Cafè d’idees’: “No podemos hacer nuestro trabajo”
articles.standfirst: La periodista reivindica: "Los periodistas somos considerados servicios esenciales..."
articles.summary: La periodista reivindica: "Los periodistas somos considerados servicios esenciales..."
articles.body: Los medios de comunicación también han contado con incidencias distintas, pero una de las que más ha impactado ha sido la que ha sucedido en el espacio de TVE en Cataluña con el programa de Gemma Nierga y ha ocurrido en pleno directo. Un piquete ha entrado en el plató y provocado que el programa no pudiera seguir con su habitual transcurrir. Un grupo de manifestantes ha irrumpido en el plató de 'Cafè d'idees', el programa presentado en La 2 Cat, obligando a interrumpir la emisión en directo pese a contar con los servicios mínimos establecidos para la jornada. Ahora bien, Nierga ha denunciado públicamente que el piquete estaba impidiendo el trabajo de los periodistas. "Este programa había preparado un programa especial, pero no podemos hacer nuestro trabajo porque un grupo de manifestantes ha accedido al plató impidiendo que ejerzamos nuestro derecho a informar y que vosotros tengáis el derecho a recibir información", ha señalado en ese instante. Además, la periodista se ha lamentado porque considera el papel esencial de los medios de comunicación durante las jornadas de huelga. "Los periodistas somos considerados servicios esenciales, pero no podemos hacer nuestro trabajo". Esto provocaba la obligación a suspender temporalmente el programa de Nierga, cuya cuenta oficial ha confirmado que la emisión estaba siendo alterada por dichas movilizaciones en el plató concretamente. Alrededor de las 8:45 horas, después de unos 45 minutos de interrupción, 'Cafè d'idees' ha podido recuperar su programación en directo.

articles.title: Sidharth Malhotra was unbothered about Kiara Advani's intimate scenes with Yash in 'Toxic', says the actress as she breaks silence on the controversy and trolling: 'Been happening...from Aishwarya to many actresses'
articles.summary: Kiara Advani has finally breaks silence on the backlash she faced over her intimate scenes with Yash in ‘Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups’, admitting
articles.body: Kiara Advani has finally breaks silence on the backlash she faced over her intimate scenes with Yash in ‘Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups’, admitting that the film's initial response left her emotionally disappointed. The actor discussed the experience during her appearance on ‘Koffee With Karan Season 9’, where she was accompanied by her husband, Sidharth Malhotra. The episode also saw the couple speak about their personal life, including the news of their second pregnancy, which they announced in early October 2026.Speaking to host Karan Johar about the film's box-office performance and audience response, Kiara admitted that she found it difficult to deal with the reaction during the opening weekend. Despite the film getting off to a strong start, its reception did not match the team's expectations. Recalling how she felt, she said, “On day one, it is heartbreaking. Especially for this film, because as a team in totality any of us saw this coming. When it misfired despite it opening to what it did. It was heartbreaking for me that first weekend. I was very low about it,”However, the actor also spoke about the positive feedback she received for stepping outside her comfort zone and taking up a role that was different from her previous performances. She added, “But, then, there was a lot of appreciation. The fact that I had gone outside of my comfort zone playing that role. I think in my journey this will be defining.”The conversation also touched upon the controversy surrounding the song ‘Tabaahi’, following which Kiara faced considerable trolling over her intimate scenes with Yash. Several social media users questioned her decision to perform such scenes, bringing her marriage and motherhood into the discussion. Sidharth Malhotra was also dragged into the controversy, with many speculating about how he would have reacted to watching his wife in intimate scenes with another actor.Karan Johar pointed out the gender bias behind such reactions, highlighting how married male actors are seldom subjected to similar scrutiny for performing intimate scenes on screen. Responding to the discussion, Kiara made it clear that Sidharth was never bothered by the controversy and had not even brought up the subject with her. She said, “He had not cared about it. He has never brought it up. We have never spoken about it. It did not affect him, he was not bothered,”The actor also observed that women in the film industry have been subjected to such judgement for years, pointing out that several actresses before her have faced similar scrutiny. Referring to the larger pattern, she said, “It has been happening now for donkey years, for decades. From Aishwarya to so many wonderful actors,”Interestingly, Kiara revealed that she did not feel compelled to justify her choices or respond to the criticism. She was also encouraged by the number of people who called out the hypocrisy surrounding the backlash. Explaining her approach, she said, "What I must touch upon is when I was seeing what was going on the internet, there was a massive reaction of people who had already started calling it out, the hypocrisy, and I really did not feel the need to even justify,"Directed by Geetu Mohandas, ‘Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups’ marked Yash's first film after the success of ‘KGF: Chapter 2’. Set in post-independence Goa, the gangster drama explores a world of crime, violence, power struggles and shifting loyalties. Yash plays two characters, Raya and his son Rumi, while Kiara portrays Nadia, Rumi's mother.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Brandon Sklenar got 'massive' to play a Delta Force operator in Taylor Sheridan's 'F.A.S.T.'
articles.summary: Brandon Sklenar reveals he got "massive" to play a Delta Force operator in Taylor Sheridan's "F.A.S.T.," a DEA black op thriller for Warners.
articles.body: Brandon Sklenar is shining a light on his transformation for the upcoming movie "F.A.S.T." The film is being made by "Yellowstone" creator Taylor Sheridan, and while not a lot of details are known, the publicly released plot is pretty epic. It's stated as follows: JOSH BROLIN CONFIRMS SICARIO 3 'IS HAPPENING' AS TAYLOR SHERIDAN FRANCHISE PREPARES TO RETURN F.A.S.T. concerns a former special forces commando, down on his luck after he returns Stateside, who is tapped by the DEA to lead a black op strike team against CIA-protected drug dealers in his town. TAYLOR SHERIDAN HAS WRITTEN THE SCRIPT FOR 'SICARIO 3' AS FRANCHISE GEARS UP FOR RETURN Sounds like it's right up the alley of anyone who loved "Sicario," and Sklenar will lead the way. Brandon Sklenar talks transformation for upcoming Taylor Sheridan movie. Sklenar spoke with "The Hollywood Reporter" about the upcoming movie, which is scheduled to premiere in May 2027, and revealed he had to bulk up for the role. "I put on a bunch of size for another film I had done earlier in the year. I’m starring in this film Taylor Sheridan wrote called F.A.S.T. for Warners. It’s coming out in May. I played a Delta Force operator, and I got massive," the former "1923" star told the outlet. What's interesting about Sklenar's comments is one very simple fact: Most Tier One operators (the U.S. military has five Tier One units), do not look anything like bodybuilders. In fact, I know several former operators who are fairly short and wiry. Being a massive person with a bodybuilder physique isn't overly advantageous when you need to ruck through mountains or blend in during low visibility operations. SEAL TEAM 6 MEMBER EXPLAINS BLUNT REALITY OF COMBAT AND EXPECTATIONS IN THE BLACK OPS WORLD Hollywood, for reasons that will never make sense to me, decides to portray commandos as if they're all physical super humans. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER There are Delta Force commandos who look like your local accountant or the science teacher at your nearby high school. There were multiple members of the operation to kill Osama bin Laden who didn't come close to cracking 6'0", including the mysterious point man going up to the third deck. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Having said all that, I am very excited to see what Sheridan delivers with "F.A.S.T." We'll find out in May 2027. articles.title: Antonio Sabato Jr and Virginia Madsen's son arrested in fatal hit-and-run
articles.summary: Jack Sabato, son of Antonio Sabato Jr. and Virginia Madsen, faces felony charges after a fatal hit-and-run in Anchorage, Alaska, police say.
articles.body: Antonio Sabato Jr. and Virginia Madsen’s son, Jack Sabato, has been arrested in connection with a fatal hit-and-run in Anchorage, Alaska, Fox News Digital has confirmed. According to the Anchorage Police Department, Sabato, 32, was arrested Nov. 9 on charges of leaving the scene of an accident without assisting the injured and leaving the scene of an accident resulting in injury or death. Police identified the victim as Carl Simmonds, 42, who was pronounced dead after officers and medics responded to reports of an unresponsive man near Airport Heights Drive and Debarr Road around 5:48 a.m. A preliminary investigation indicated a vehicle struck Simmonds and fled the scene, police said. VIRGINIA MADSEN SAYS VETERANS AREN'T TRAINED TO COME HOME AFTER NEPHEW'S SUICIDE According to court records obtained by Fox News Digital, Jack has been hit with a felony charge of leaving the scene of an accident without helping the victim, as well as a misdemeanor charge of leaving the scene of an accident involving injury or death. Charging documents reviewed by Alaska Public Media reported that responding officers found Simmonds' body on the sidewalk off Airport Heights Drive and several car parts scattered around. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS While reviewing security footage from a nearby bank, officers saw a white Chevy Tahoe striking Simmonds and not braking before or after the crash, according to the outlet. After running the vehicle’s description into the Alaska Public Safety Information Network, law enforcement found the matching vehicle — which is registered to Jack — parked at the Anchorage Amazon warehouse. The vehicle was then seized. He said he believed he hit an animal and didn’t stop because he was driving without insurance. He also said he ran a red light because he felt unsafe driving without headlights. He said he planned to report the crash after work but contacted police after his girlfriend told him his SUV had been seized, saying he "knew the worst," according to the documents. articles.title: Kelsey Grammer still feels 'sense of smallness' for not serving in military: 'I do my best to make up for it'
articles.summary: Kelsey Grammer's giant screen film, "America the Beautiful," celebrates national parks and military sacrifice ahead of its Veterans Day premiere.
articles.body: Kelsey Grammer feels he missed an opportunity to give back to his country by not serving in the military when he was younger. During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 71-year-old actor discussed his latest project, "America the Beautiful," a 40-minute giant screen documentary, and why he always does his best to "show up for the military" when he is able to. "I will always have an annoying sort of sense of smallness that I didn't serve, but I do my best to make up for it," he said. He explained that, despite feeling that way, he is unsure if he would have made a different decision if given the opportunity to do his life over again, noting, "It was a really interesting time." HOLLYWOOD MARINE VETERAN ROB RIGGLE DOUBTS MODERN STARS WOULD MAKE JIMMY STEWART'S WWII SACRIFICE WATCH: Kelsey Grammer feels a ‘sense of smallness’ for not having served in the military When he was a young man, he said, the Vietnam War was "sort of in full flair," and he had signed up for the draft and was ready to go fight had his number been drawn, but "President Nixon pulled us out just before I would have gone down to get my number." "So, I was thankful for not having to go, make that decision, but I would've gone. If my number had been up, I woulda gone. But I was, I was thankful not to," he said. "I used to work in San Diego. It was one of my first jobs at the Shakespeare Festival there, and I would go over to the Point Loma Military Graveyard and have a lunch sometimes. And I'd sit next to this cross that I'd found of a young man who was really only eight months older than I was who had died in Vietnam. And it just broke my heart." As a father, Grammer says he speaks to his children about the many sacrifices people have made to ensure the safety of America, adding he "will always try and instruct them with the idea that service to your country is a good idea." KELSEY GRAMMER WARNS OF CHILLING DANGER FACING AMERICANS WHO FORGET NATION'S FOUNDING HISTORY WATCH: Kelsey Grammer’s grandfather was an ‘inspiration’ to him He says that together they discuss the Revolutionary War and all the great battles throughout history, noting he would encourage them to serve their country if they wanted to, but "their mom would get mad at me." He noted, however, that this is something "people have been doing" for many years. "There's a lot of wonderful patriotic people in our country today whose children and whose husbands and wives are serving, and my hat is off to them all. And we salute them. I mean, with this particular thing, the 11 hour, the 11 day, 11th month, Armistice Day originally, now Veterans Day at the end of the first World War. Remarkable. The number of people who died in that war," he said. "So, certainly the hope was that it would never happen again and, sure enough, a generation later, we were fighting World War II. Amazing. And we go on. We continue. Hopefully it'll end one day." Grammer feels a strong connection to Veterans Day since his grandfather served as a colonel in the Army Corps of Engineers during World War II. When speaking about his grandfather, the "Frasier" star said he "was always an inspiration to me." "I looked up to him like a kid would," he said. "I mean, he raised me, but his bravery and his courage and his commitment to the country, these were active, living, breathing things that he was … he embodied that. And, so, it's always been my hope to kind of pass that along a little bit. At least a remembrance of him, respect for what he was able to do in the face of extraordinary hardship." CARRIE UNDERWOOD, GARY SINISE LEAD STARS WHO'VE SHARED WHY THEY'RE PROUD TO BE AMERICANS One way in which Grammer is honoring his grandfather — and all the other men and women who have served the country — is through his new film, "America the Beautiful," which hits screens Nov. 11. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE The film was created in honor of America's 250th birthday and celebrates the beauty of the country and the love of the land Americans share for it. WATCH: Kelsey Grammer’s new documentary, ‘America the Beautiful,’ showcases the beauty of the country "That was the original idea of the movie, why they made it, and they invited me to join in. I think it's absolutely apropos. I mean, without the sacrifices that have been made by our military men and women, then we might not actually have this treasure of national beauty that we do have," he said. "The Americans that have gotten to know our national forests and our national parks. They are inspired by them every day and blessed by the fact that they're still here. And I think that speaks in large part of the sacrifices that people make abroad and at home to secure our future and to defend our country." Through making the film, he was able to understand President Theodore Roosevelt's philosophy that "we have to preserve our physical life as well as our creative and our ideological life." He learned how Roosevelt was allotted "time to seek solace in nature" and gather inspiration and comfort from it, leading him to create the national park system, believing "everybody should be able to have" the same "personal relationship with the wilderness" as he found. Grammer's hope for the film is that audiences are able to understand the "overwhelming beauty we have been given" in this country, calling it "powerful" and saying "it defines us." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Of all the places he visited, he called the Badlands his favorite, saying, "I felt like I was in a holy place" while he was there, saying it felt like being "in God's land." "It was just an amazing day we spent there and, of course, then we went and saw Mount Rushmore. We also saw on the way there … a mountain called a Crazy Horse, which is like four times bigger than Mount Rushmore," he said. "It's an amazing thing that a private family's been working on it for 60 years, maybe longer, where it's just Crazy Horse seated on his steed, and he says, with his finger pointing outwards, sort of like this, he says, ‘My lands are where my dead lie buried.’ WATCH: Kelsey Grammer hopes viewers see ‘the overwhelming beauty we have been given’ in new documentary "And that's powerful stuff, but I think that is an American saying. That is an American occurrence. It's these two cultures clashed, and then he became a new culture together, but it's all based on that land, this extraordinary land that we have. "And, yeah, it's a rainbow. It's a cornucopia of life and teaming, teaming life, renewal, power, all these things that actually really are America. They live here, and I'm proud to have done the movie." articles.title: Pablo Motos apunta a Pedro Sánchez por no querer dar la cara en 'El Hormiguero': "Cobardía y España envenenada"
articles.standfirst: El presentador del programa de Antena 3 carga contra el jefe del Ejecutivo tras no recibir respuesta a la invitación a su programa con motivo del 29N
articles.summary: El presentador del programa de Antena 3 carga contra el jefe del Ejecutivo tras no recibir respuesta a la invitación a su programa con motivo del 29N
articles.body: Este miércoles, 11 de noviembre, ‘El Hormiguero’, espacio que presenta y dirige Pablo Motos en el ‘access prime time’ de Antena 3, recibió a Alberto Núñez Feijóo, líder del Partido Popular (PP), con motivo de las próximas elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre (29N). Sin embargo, antes de proceder a la charla con el máximo responsable de la formación azul, mandó un contundente mensaje a Pedro Sánchez, presidente del Gobierno, al no atender su llamada para acudir al programa. “Quiero aclarar que exactamente igual que en las anteriores elecciones, (nosotros hemos llamado a los dos principales candidatos que tienen opciones reales de gobernar este país, y uno de ellos no se ha presentado. Le hemos insistido al candidato Pedro Sánchez durante más de un mes, llamando cada día, mandando mensajes para que quedase por escrito, dándole todas las opciones posibles para venir, pero ha decidido no hacerlo”, comenzó diciendo al respecto. Motos cree que es una “torpeza” política porque hay “miles” de votos y por otro, afirma que es “cobardía”. Asimismo, el presentador de ‘El Hormiguero’ enumeró lo que le hubiera gustado preguntarle al actual jefe del Ejecutivo para que se explicase “bien” y “con tiempo”: ¿Por qué se fue de vacaciones 24 días mientras estaban invadiendo nuestro país?”. “Me hubiese gustado preguntarle si pone la mano en el fuego por Zapatero. Me hubiese gustado preguntarle si está a favor o en contra de los okupas. Me hubiese gustado preguntarle quién le habrá pagado a Leire para que contacte con unos narcotraficantes para eliminar a la jueza que iba a juzgar a su hermano, y sobre si no son ellos no la demandan”, siguió manifestando. “También me hubiese gustado preguntarle por Ábalos, por las prostitutas, por Cerdán, por Koldo, y cómo es posible que yendo con ellos un año en el mismo coche no se enterase de nada. Me hubiese gustado preguntarle por Puigdemont, me hubiese gustado preguntarle por el Sáhara, y cuál se supone que es el beneficio que hemos sacado de esa operación”, señaló. Finalmente, el comunicador de Requena hizo mención a los afectados en los desastres que afectaron a nuestro país, con un claro mensaje hacia su Gobierno: “Me hubiese gustado preguntarle por qué siempre que hay un problema real donde hay que ser eficaz como la DANA, el volcán de La Palma, el accidente de Adamuz, el accidente de Urda o la invasión de Ceuta, los ciudadanos se sienten absolutamente abandonados a su suerte mientras el Gobierno dice que lo está haciendo todo bien”. “Me hubiese gustado preguntarle si esta España con todo el mundo envenenado es la España con la que él soñaba”, sentenció.

articles.title: Lori Loughlin's daughter Olivia Jade showcases her toned figure in pink string bikini
articles.summary: Olivia Jade's pink bikini photos drew praise from fans and a fire emoji from mom Lori Loughlin, while Victoria Justice called her "stunning."
articles.body: Olivia Jade is bringing the summer heat with a new set of photos on Instagram. In a recent Instagram post, the 27-year-old influencer shared a series of photos of herself in a pink Monday Swimwear string bikini, captioning the post, "Sunshine girl 🎀🎀🎀🎀." One of the photos features the YouTuber showing off her toned body as she leaned against a wooden fence, with green hillsides and a river behind her. Other photos show her posing in front of a white wall. She accessorized the look with a pair of black sunglasses and earrings, and wore her hair in a messy low bun. LORI LOUGHLIN AND DAUGHTER OLIVIA JADE STUN ON RED CARPET AS FANS CAN'T GET OVER THEIR RESEMBLANCE Fans in the comments section could not help but compliment the influencer, with one writing, "Okay pretty girl!!!," and another adding, "Perfect body 🔥." "It's almost like Aunt Becky went back in time and became a VS model," a third commenter added. Her mom, "Full House" star Lori Loughlin, also got in on the action, leaving a fire emoji in the comments section, while "Victorious" actress, Victoria Justice wrote, "Stunning🔥." Jade recently went viral for participating in a campaign with the clothing brand, Reformation. In the campaign, she posed in a crewneck sweater with the word "college" written on it, with "100% of the net proceeds from the" sale of the sweater going to Yes Scholars, a nonprofit aimed towards helping students from under-resourced communities with access to college and other opportunities. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Her involvement in the campaign drew praise from fans, with some writing in the comments section that she is "making lemonade with lemons," and another calling the move "iconic." Jade was infamously exposed for having lied on her college applications and pretending to be on the rowing team, in order to secure admission into USC. This became public in 2019, when news of the college admissions scandal broke, implicating her parents. Loughlin and Jade's father, Mossimo Giannulli, paid $500,000 to scam mastermind William "Rick" Singer to get her and her sister, Isabella, recruited to the University of Southern California’s crew team despite neither girl previously participating in the sport. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? Loughlin on the other hand served two months in prison, paid a $150,000 fine, with two years of supervised release and 100 hours of community service. articles.title: In 1986, Henry Winkler directed Dolly Parton’s first TV movie; after her passing, he revealed how her ‘Trash’ became an unexpected souvenir on set
articles.summary: Back in 1986, Henry Winkler was directing Dolly Parton’s first made-for-TV movie, ‘A Smoky Mountain Christmas’.
articles.body: Back in 1986, Henry Winkler was directing Dolly Parton’s first made-for-TV movie, ‘A Smoky Mountain Christmas’. Decades later, at Rhode Island Comic Con in November, the ‘Happy Days’ star still lights up talking about that production and the country legend who starred in it.The story he told the crowd is pure Hollywood oddity: how Dolly’s “trash” became a souvenir no one was supposed to take.The scene that set it up, as revealed by Henry WinklerWinkler was answering questions during a ‘Happy Days’ panel at the Omni Providence Hotel, as reported by People, sharing the stage with his old co-star Anson Williams. He drifted into memories of directing the 1986 holiday fantasy. In one sequence, Dolly’s character, a famous country singer named Lorna Davis, gets kidnapped. Police officers search her apartment looking for clues.One of the actors playing a cop spoke up on set. He wanted something to remember the job by. “I would love to take a souvenir. What can I take?” he asked. Winkler shut it down immediately. “Anything you take would be stealing,” he told the actor. That was the rule. No props walking off the lot.The boom mic operator’s clever fix to Henry WinklerThe boom microphone operator working that same scene had a different idea. Dolly’s character had been writing music. She crumpled the paper and tossed it into a trash can. The operator pointed it out: that crumpled sheet was headed for the garbage anyway. Why not let the actor take one of those? “It was gonna be trash anyway. You could take that,” the mic operator said, according to Winkler.The actor walked away with a piece of paper Dolly had handled, written on, and discarded in character. Winkler still smiles at the memory. “And that was my experience with Dolly.”Henry Winkler working with a force of natureThe keepsake story is only part of what Winkler wanted the Comic Con audience to understand. He spoke about Dolly herself with clear affection and respect. “She was everything you can imagine she was and more,” he said.“The most amazing star; she just was a powerful being on this earth. Truly, I was honoured to direct her first television movie.”‘A Smoky Mountain Christmas’ was exactly that, her first film made for television. According to IMDb, the story follows a country-western singer travelling through the Tennessee mountains who crosses paths with a reclusive backwoodsman and a witch.Lee Majors, Bo Hopkins, and Dan Hedaya rounded out the cast. For Winkler, the experience went beyond the finished product. Directing Dolly left a lasting impression of her presence, her work ethic, and the way she filled a room.A story that still travelsNearly forty years later, Winkler is still telling the tale with the same warmth. The Rhode Island Comic Con appearance was not a formal tribute. It was simply a conversation that wandered back to an old set, a strict rule about props, and one creative workaround that let an actor leave with something personal.Dolly Parton died on August 25 at the age of 80. Winkler’s remarks arrive months later, not as a formal memorial but as a lived memory shared in front of fans who grew up with both of them on their screens.More on Henry WinklerHenry Winkler remains one of those rare performers whose career has never really settled into one chapter. Born in New York in 1945 to German-Jewish immigrant parents, he first became a household name in the 1970s as Arthur 'Fonzie' Fonzarelli on ‘Happy Days’.The leather jacket and the catchphrase made him a cultural fixture, yet he kept pushing past the typecasting. He directed television, including ‘A Smoky Mountain Christmas’, appeared in films ranging from ‘The Waterboy’ to the ‘Scream’ series, and later earned critical praise and an Emmy for his role as the eccentric acting coach Gene Cousineau in ‘Barry’.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
